# Text Rendering Notes

## Categories of text

1. **Point annotation labels** — name displayed alongside a POI icon (e.g. "Children's Fairyland")
2. **Icon-less POI text** — POIs with no icon that are represented as text only (e.g. "Knowland Park", parks, preserves, open space)
3. **Road labels** — names that follow road geometry along the polyline
4. **Area / region labels** — oceans, bays, large named regions; may overlap with category 2

## Visual hierarchy

Text size and weight vary by importance. City names are larger; minor POIs are smaller. Water bodies and natural features conventionally use italic. Font weight also signals hierarchy (bold for cities, regular for local POIs).

## Renderer approach

Custom Three.js text renderer using a signed distance field (SDF) font atlas. SDF rendering allows crisp scaling at any size and makes halos essentially free — render the atlas twice with a wider threshold for the halo pass.

## Halos / outlines

Non-negotiable for readability on a photorealistic background. Must be designed into the SDF shader from the start, not added later.

## Collision / screen occupation

The existing occupation manager uses point radii. Text requires rectangular (AABB) bounds, and road labels require rotated rectangle (OBB) bounds. The occupation manager will need to handle both shapes, or a separate collision layer is needed for text.

## Line breaking

Area labels need a maximum width, line-break logic, and vertical centering within the polygon bounds (e.g. "Bay National / Wildlife / Refuge").

## Road labels

Glyphs are laid out individually along the road polyline — a fundamentally different placement model from billboard text. Treat as a separate sub-problem.

## `min_zoom`

A Web Mercator build-time concept. Redundant as a load-time filter (the tile generator already excludes features below their `min_zoom` from coarser tiles). Potentially useful as a zoom-out visual consistency gate: when the camera pulls back and fine tiles are still resident, `min_zoom` can identify features that have "aged out" of their appropriate zoom range and should be proactively removed from the occupancy grid before tile unload catches up. No equivalent utility when zooming in.

## Parent LoD feature retention

Point annotation features from parent (coarser) LoD tiles are safe to display at finer zoom levels — there is no `max_zoom`, so importance-filtered point features remain valid at any zoom. Area and road labels are not safe to retain from parent LoDs: area label centers may be off-screen at fine zoom, and coarse road geometry produces incorrect path-following label placement.

## Deferred

- Road label rendering and curved glyph placement
- Area label polygon centroid placement and off-screen handling
- Generalized geometry replacement at LoD transitions
- Bidirectional / RTL text support
- Language / locale selection (`name` vs `name:en`)
